title: Pediatric Severe Febrile Illness with Danger Signs
guidelines: WHO Integrated Management of Childhood Illness (IMCI)
NICE Guideline NG143: Fever in under 5s
pathophysiology: Acute systemic pediatric infection with dehydration and physiological compromise.

facts.onset: The caregiver reports the 2-year-old child developed high fever yesterday, became irritable, and refused to drink milk or water this morning.
facts.symptoms: Vomiting everything taken, high pitch crying, poor urine output (dry diaper for 8 hours).
facts.history: Child is 2 years old, weight 12 kg. Immunizations up to date. No known drug allergies.
facts.risk: Lethargic, drowsy, difficult to wake up, breathing fast.
facts.exam: Child is irritable, drowsy, with sunken eyes and dry mucous membranes. Capillary refill time is 4 seconds. Mild subcostal indrawing. No stiff neck or petechial rash.

blood-glucose.name: Point-of-care Blood Glucose
blood-glucose.interpretation: Risk of pediatric hypoglycemia secondary to poor oral intake and high metabolic demand.
blood-glucose.why: Immediate rule-out of hypoglycemia in any lethargic or unwell pediatric patient.

blood-culture.name: Pediatric Blood Culture
blood-culture.result: Sample collected before parenteral antimicrobials; pending incubation.
blood-culture.interpretation: Essential baseline to identify bacteremia or invasive bacterial disease.
blood-culture.why: Identify bloodstream infection before starting empiric antibiotics.

fbc.name: Full Blood Count (Micro-sample)
fbc.result: WBC 22.8 x 10^9/L with left shift (neutrophils 82%); Platelets 260 x 10^9/L; Hb 11.4 g/dL.
fbc.interpretation: Marked leukocytosis supporting invasive bacterial infection.
fbc.why: Assess systemic inflammatory response in severe pediatric febrile illness.

lumbar-puncture.name: Lumbar Puncture (CSF analysis)
lumbar-puncture.result: Deferred until clinical stabilization; no immediate signs of raised intracranial pressure, but child must be resuscitated first.
lumbar-puncture.interpretation: Indicated if meningitis suspected once airway and hemodynamics are secure.
lumbar-puncture.why: Investigate central nervous system infection once stable.

ct-head.name: CT Head
ct-head.result: Not performed; child has no focal neurological signs, open fontanelle considerations, or trauma history.
ct-head.interpretation: Unnecessary ionizing radiation in a 2-year-old without focal neurological indications.
ct-head.why: Avoid pediatric radiation hazard; bedside stabilization and infectious workup take priority.

expected_actions: Immediate assessment of pediatric ABCDE and danger signs (inability to drink, vomiting everything, convulsions, lethargy)
Targeted IV/IO access and weight-based fluid bolus (10-20 mL/kg isotonic crystalloid) over 15-30 minutes
Immediate IV broad-spectrum antimicrobials (e.g., Ceftriaxone 80 mg/kg or Cefotaxime)
Monitor capillary blood glucose and correct hypoglycemia if < 3.0 mmol/L
Urgent escalation to Pediatric Consultant / Senior Pediatric Emergency Team
critical_errors: Administering adult drug doses without precise weight-based calculation in a pediatric patient
Missing pediatric general danger signs (lethargy, inability to drink, persistent vomiting)
Delaying resuscitation to perform imaging or lumbar puncture in an unstable child
